questions.q: A gaseous compounds having carbon, hydrogen and oxygen was burnt in the presence of oxygen. After combustion, 1 volume of the gaseous compound produces 2 volumes of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and 2 volumes of steam. questions.solution:
Suppose the chemical formula of the compound be $\mathrm{C}_x \mathrm{H}_y \mathrm{O}_z$ chemical reaction related to combustion of the compound.

Since, 2 molecules of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ have 2 atoms of carbon and these carbon must have come from the compound. Hence, the value of $x$ is 2 . questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The points on the curve $x y^2=1$ which are nearest to the origin, are
questions.solution:
Let $P(x, y)$ be such a point, then
$O P^2=x^2+y^2$
Let
$s=O P^2=x^2+\frac{1}{x}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d s}{d x}=2 x-\frac{1}{x^2}$
For maximum or minimum, put $\frac{d s}{d x}=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 x-\frac{1}{x^2}=0 \Rightarrow x^3=\frac{1}{2}\therefore \quad x=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$
Also, $\quad \frac{d^2 s}{d x^2}=2+\frac{2}{x^3}$
Now, $\left(\frac{d^2 s}{d x^2}\right)_{x=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{1 / 3}}=2+\frac{2}{1 / 2}\gt0\therefore s$ is minimum at $x=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{1 / 3}$.
Thus, for nearest point $x=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{1 / 3}$,
$y= \pm\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-1 / 6}$

Given, $\sin A \sin B=\frac{a b}{c^2}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow c^2=\frac{a b}{\sin A \sin B}=\left(\frac{a}{\sin A}\right)\left(\frac{b}{\sin B}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow c^2=\left(\frac{c}{\sin C}\right)^2 \quad\left[\because \frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & \sin ^2 C & =1 \\ \Rightarrow & & C & =90^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Hence, $\triangle A B C$ is a right angled triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $2 a+3 b+6 c=0$, then atleast one root of the equation $a x^2+b x+c=0$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
Consider the function
$f(x)=\frac{a x^3}{3}+\frac{b x^2}{2}+c x+d$
We have, $\quad f(0)=d$
and $\quad f(1)=\frac{a}{3}+\frac{b}{2}+c+d\begin{aligned} & =\frac{2 a+3 b+6 c}{6}+d \\ & =\frac{0}{6}+d \quad[\because 2 a+3 b+6 c=0]\end{aligned}$
Therefore, 0 and 1 are roots of the polynomial $f(x)$. Hence, according to Rolle's theorem, there exists atleast one root of the polynomial $f^{\prime}(x)=a x^2+b x+c$ lying between 0 and 1.

Thus, we have to find the equation of the plane passing through $\mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and normal to the vector $\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{n}_1 \times \mathbf{n}_2$.
The equation of the required plane is
$(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{a}) \cdot \mathbf{n}$ or $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{n}=\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{n}$
or $\mathbf{r} \cdot(-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+7 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+13 \hat{\mathbf{k}})=(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \cdot(-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+7 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+13 \hat{\mathbf{k}})$

questions.q: A vector perpendicular to the plane containing the points $A(1,-1,2), B(2,0,-1)$, $C(0,2,1)$ is
questions.solution:
We know that a vector perpendicular to the plane containing the point $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ is given by $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}+\mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{C}+\mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{A}$.
Given, $\mathbf{A}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}, \quad=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+0 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
and $\mathbf{C}=0 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Now, $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{array}\right|=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{C}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{array}\right|=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{A}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right|=5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Thus, $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}+\mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{C}+\mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{A}\begin{aligned} & =(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+(5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ & =8 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A sphere of mass $m$ moving with a constant velocity $u$ hits another stationary sphere of the same mass. If $e$ is the coefficient of restitution, then the ratio of velocities of the two spheres after collision $\left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)$ will be
questions.solution:
Conservation of momentum (gives)
$m u+0=m v_1+m v_2\Rightarrow \quad v_1+v_2=u\ldots$ (i)
Newton's experimental formula,
$v_1-v_2=-e\left[u_1-u_2\right] \text { gives }v_1-v_2=-e u\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$v_1=\frac{(1-e) u}{2}v_2=\frac{(1+e) u}{2}\therefore \quad \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\frac{1-e}{1+e}$

questions.q: The wavelength of incident light falling on a photosensitive surface is changed from $2000 Å$ to $2100 Å$. The corresponding change in stopping potential is
questions.solution:

Change in stopping potential

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a planetary motion, the areal velocity of position vector of a planet depends on angular velocity ( $\omega$ ) and distance $(r)$ of the planet from the sun. The correct relation for areal velocity $\left(\frac{d A}{d t}\right)$ is

questions.q: The molar specific heat of oxygen at constant pressure $C_p=7.03 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $R=8.31 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The amount of heat taken by 5 moles of oxygen when heated at constant volume from $10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ will be approximately.
questions.solution:
Given, $C_p=7.03 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, R=8.315 / \mathrm{mol}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$,
$\begin{gathered}n=5 \text { moles, } T_2=20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, T_1=10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, \\ \Delta Q=?\end{gathered}\therefore$ Heat, $\Delta Q=n C_V \Delta T=n\left(C_p-R\right) \Delta T \quad\left[\because C_p-C_V=R\right]\begin{aligned} & =5\left[7.03-\frac{8.31}{4.2}\right] \times(20-10) \\ & =253 \mathrm{cal}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mixture of two gases is contained in a vessel. The gas 1 is monoatomic and gas 2 is diatomic and the ratio of their molecular masses $M_1 / M_2=1 / 4$. What is the ratio of root mean square speeds of the molecules of two gases?
questions.solution:
From kinetic theory of gases
$p=\frac{1}{3} \frac{M}{V} \cdot e^2$
Since, $p$ and $V$ are constant (same)
$\therefore \quad M_1 e_1^2=M_2 e_2^2\Rightarrow \quad \frac{e_1^2}{e_2^2}=\frac{M_2}{M_1}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{e_1}{e_2}=\sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}}=\sqrt{4 / 1}=2 \quad\left[\right.$ given, $\left.\frac{M_1}{M_2}=\frac{1}{4}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the system shown in figure $M_1 \gt M_2$ and pulley and threads are ideal. System is held at rest by thread $B C$. Just after thread $B C$ is burnt.
options: Magnitude of acceleration of both masses will be $\frac{M_1-M_2}{M_1+M_2} g$
Acceleration of $M_1$ and $M_2$ will be equal to zero
Acceleration of $M_1$ will be equal to zero, which that of $M_2$ will be $\frac{M_1-M_2}{M_2} g$ upward
questions.solution:
As $M_1 \gt M_2$, so tension in thread connecting the block $B$ and support $C$ is $\left(M_1-M_2\right) g$. When this thread is burnt, this tension disappears. In this case tension in spring is $M_1 g$ and it is elongated. So, tension in string connecting $A$ and $B$ is $M_1 g$. Hence, resultant force on $A$ remains zero because tension in string is balanced by tension in spring. The block $B$ has a net upward force $\left(M_1-M_2\right) g$, so initial acceleration of block $B$ is
$\frac{\left(M_1-M_2\right) g}{M_2}$
Thus, initial acceleration of $M_1$ is zero and that of $M_2$ is $\frac{\left(M_1-M_2\right) g}{M_2}$ upward.

questions.q: Two blocks $A$ and $B$ are placed one over the other on a smooth horizontal surface. The maximum horizontal force that can be applied on the upper block $B$, so that $A$ and $B$ move without separation is 49 N . The coefficient of friction between $A$ and $B$ is

Radius of the double loop, $r=\frac{R}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two bar magnets having same geometry with magnetic moments $m$ and $2 m$, are firstly placed in such a way that their similar poles one are on same side. Then, its time period of oscillation is $T_1$. Now, the polarity of the one of the magnet is reversed. Then, time period of oscillation is $T_2$, then
questions.solution:
When similar poles are on same side time period of oscillation $T_1$ is given by
$T_1=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I_1+I_2}{\left(m_1+m_2\right) B_H}}$ [given]
$m_1=2 m, m_2=mT_1=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I_1+I_2}{(3 m) B_H}}\ldots$ (i)
When the polarity of magnet is reversed, time period of oscillation $T_2$ is given by
$T_2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I_1+I_2}{\left(m_1-m_2\right) B_H}}T_2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I_1+I_2}{m B_H}}\ldots$ (ii)
On comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$T_2 \gt T_1$
or $T_1 \lt T_2$

questions.q: A stone is projected from the ground with velocity $50 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ at an angle $30^{\circ}$ with horizontal. It crosses a wall after 3 s . How far beyond the wall the stone will strike the ground? ( $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
Time, $\begin{aligned} T & =\frac{2 u \sin \theta}{g} \\ T & =\frac{2 \times 50 \times \sin 30^{\circ}}{10}\end{aligned}=\frac{2 \times 50 \times \frac{1}{2}}{10}=5 \mathrm{~s}$
Time spent after crossing the wall, $t_2=5-3=2 \mathrm{~s}\begin{aligned}\therefore \text { Distance, } x_2 & =u \cos \theta \times 1_2 \\& =50 \times \cos 30^{\circ} \times 2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =50 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 2 \\ & =50 \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =50 \times 1.73 \\ & =86.5 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile has the maximum range 500 m . If the projectile is thrown up an inclined plane of $30^{\circ}$ with the same (magnitude) velocity, the distance covered by it along the inclined plane will be
questions.solution:
Since, range is maximum, therefore $\theta=45^{\circ}$. Hence, using $R=u^2 \sin 2 \theta / g$.
We find $500=\frac{u^2}{g}$, i.e. $u=[500 g]^{\frac{1}{2}}$.
Distance covered along the inclined plane can be obtained using relation
$v^2-v_0^2=2 a x\Rightarrow \quad 0-u^2=2 \times\left(-g \sin 30^{\circ}\right) \times x\left[\because a=-g \sin 30^{\circ}\right]\therefore \quad x=\frac{u^2}{g}=500 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: Nuclear reactor in which U-235 is used as fuel. Uses 2 kg of $\mathrm{U}-235$ in 30 days. Then, power output of the reactor will be (given energy released per fission $=185 \mathrm{MeV}$ )

Number of atoms in 2 kg of uranium

$\begin{aligned} & =5.12 \times 10^{24} \times 185 \mathrm{MeV} \\ & =5.12 \times 10^{24} \times 185 \times 10^6 \mathrm{eV}\end{aligned}$
Energy obtained per second
$=\frac{5.12 \times 10^{24} \times 185 \times 10^6 \times 16 \times 10^{-19}}{30 \times 24 \times 60 \times 60}$
Solving the above expression
$\begin{aligned} & =58.47 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~W} \\ & \cong 58.5 \mathrm{MW}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two springs are connected to a block of mass $M$ placed on a frictionless surface as shown below. If both the springs have a spring constant $k$, then the frequency of oscillation of the block is
questions.solution:
The frequency of oscillation of a vibrating spring-block, system is given by
$v=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text {eff }}}{M}} \ldots$ (i)
Since, the springs are attached in series, each having spring constant $k$, so we have
$\frac{1}{k_{\mathrm{eff}}}=\frac{1}{k}+\frac{1}{k}=\frac{2}{k}\Rightarrow \quad k_{\text {eff }}=\frac{k}{2}$
From Eq. (i), we get $v=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text {eff }}}{M}}=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{2 M}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The path difference between two waves $y_1=a_1 \sin \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$ and $y_2=a_2 \cos \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $y_1=a_1 \sin \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$ and
$y_2=a_2 \cos \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right)=a_2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right)\therefore$ Phase of first wave, $\phi_1=\left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$
and phase of second wave, $\phi_2=\frac{\pi}{2}+\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\therefore$ Phase difference, $\Delta \phi=\phi_2-\phi_1=\frac{\pi}{2}+\phi\begin{aligned} \therefore \text { Path difference } & =\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi} \times \text { phase difference } \\ & =\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\phi\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: White light reflected at normal incidence from a soap film has minima at $6500 Å$ and maxima at $7500 Å$ in the visible region with not minimum in between. If $\mu$ is $\frac{5}{3}$ for the, thin film, the thickness of film is
questions.solution:
For minima to occur,
$2 \mu t=2 n \frac{\lambda_1}{2}\ldots$ (i)
and for maxima
$2 \mu t=(2 n-1) \frac{\lambda_2}{2}\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$(2 n-1) \lambda_2=2 n \lambda_1$
or $\quad(2 n-1) 7500=(2 n) 6500$
[given, $\lambda_2=7500 Å, \lambda_1=6500 Å$ ]
or $1500 n-7500=13000 n$
or $2000 n=7500$
or $n=3.75$
Substitution the value of ($n$) in Eq. (i), we get
$2 \times \frac{5}{3} \times t=2 \times 3.75 \times \frac{6500}{2} \times 10^{-10} \quad\left[\because \mu=\frac{5}{3}\right]\Rightarrow \quad t=7.40 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q:
A ray of light is travelling through a medium of refractive index $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ with respect to air.
When it is incident on the surface making an angle $45^{\circ}$ with the surface, which of the following will take place?
options: The ray will be internally reflected
questions.solution:
Given, $\mu=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ w.r.t. air $i=45^{\circ}, r=$ ?
Also, $\mu=\frac{\sin i}{\sin r}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{\sin r} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1 / \sqrt{2}}{\sin r}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & \sin r & =1 \\ \Rightarrow & & r & =90^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Note that the ray is incident from denser medium and is refracted into a rarer medium air.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin walled glass sphere of radius 2.5 cm is filled with water. An object $(O)$ is placed at 7.5 cm from the surface of the sphere. Neglecting the effect of glass wall, at what distance the image ( $I$ ) of the object, measured from the centre of sphere is formed?
questions.solution:
For refraction at first surface,
$u=-7.5 \mathrm{~cm}, R_1=2.5 \mathrm{~cm}\mu_1=1, \mu_2=\frac{4}{3}\therefore \quad \frac{\mu_2}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{\mu_1}{u}=\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R_1}\frac{4 / 3}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{1}{(-7.5)}=\frac{4 / 3-1}{25}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{4}{3 v^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{7.5}-\frac{1}{7.5}=0\Rightarrow \quad v^{\prime}=\infty$
It means the ray is parallel within the sphere. For refraction at second surface,
$u=-\infty, \mu_1=\frac{4}{3}\mu_2=1, R_2=-2.5 \mathrm{~cm}\therefore \quad \frac{\mu_2}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{\mu_1}{u}=\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R_2}$ gives
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{4 / 3}{(-\infty)}=\frac{1-(4 / 3)}{(-2.5)}\Rightarrow \quad v=+7.5 \mathrm{~cm}$
i.e. Image is formed at distance 7.5 cm to the right of $P_2$. Hence, distance of final image $P$ from centre $C=7.5+2.5=10 \mathrm{~cm}$.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, when wavelength used is $600 Å$ and the screen is 40 cm from the slits, then the fringes are 0.012 cm apart. What is the distance between the slits?
questions.solution:
Given, $D=40 \mathrm{~cm}=40 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}\begin{aligned} \lambda & =600 Å=6000 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m} \\ W & =0.012 \mathrm{~cm}=0.012 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}\therefore$ Fringe width,

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a wave travelling in positive $x$-direction with $A=0.2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, velocity $=360 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $\lambda=60 \mathrm{~m}$, then correct expression for the wave is
questions.solution:
General equation for a plane progressive wave travelling along positive $x$-direction is given by
$y=A \sin (\omega t-k x)=A \sin \left[2 \pi\left(v t-\frac{x}{\lambda}\right)\right]\ldots$ (i)
Here, it is given
$v=360 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \lambda=60 \mathrm{~m}$
We know that, frequency $v=\frac{v}{\lambda}=\frac{360}{60}=6 \mathrm{~Hz}$ Substituting $A=0.2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \mathrm{v}=6 \mathrm{~Hz}\begin{aligned} & \lambda=60 \mathrm{~m} \text { in Eq. (i), we get } \\ & y=0.2 \sin \left[2 \pi\left(6 t-\frac{x}{60}\right)\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A block of mass 1 kg slides down a curved track that is one quadrant of a circle of radius 1 m . Speed of the block at the bottom is $2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Work done by the frictional force on the block when it reaches at the bottom is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle moves along $X$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=5 \mathrm{~cm}$ under the influence of force given by $F=\left(7-2 x+3 x^2\right) \mathrm{N}$. The work done in the process is
questions.solution:
The given force varies with distance. Therefore, work done,
$W=\int_0^{x=5} F \cdot d x\begin{aligned} & =\int_0^5\left(7-2 x+3 x^2\right) d x \\ & =\left[7 x-\frac{2 x^2}{2}+\frac{3 x^3}{3}\right]_0^5\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\left[7 \times 5-(5)^2+(5)^3-0\right] \\ & =135 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
